newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Irish finmin sees GNP growth of 4.5 pct in 1998/99.
newsitem.headline: Irish finmin sees GNP growth of 4.5 pct in 1998/99.

text.p: Irish finance minister Ruairi Quinn said on Thursday that Ireland's GNP growth was expected to be around 5.5 percent in 1997 and 4.5 percent on average in 1998 and 1999.

"Inflation is expected to remain subdued, at slightly over two percent. Employment growth is expected to average 38,000 per year, with the increase next year somewhat higher than this average," Quinn told a parliamentary debate on his 1997 spending estimates.
He said tax cuts in his 1997 Budget would be matched with restraint on spending to prevent Ireland's fiscal policy becoming expansionary.

"Looking to the 1997 fiscal policy stance, the proposed changes in taxation, which have been discussed with the social partners, will underpin moderate wage developments, as recommended by the central bank," he said.

Quinn told a parliamentary debate on his 1997 spending estimates that the pay element of the recent wage deal between the government, employers and unions represented a continuation of the wage moderation of the past decade.
Ireland's central bank said earlier in December that low inflation requires a firm exchange rate and modest wage developments.
"I can agree with these recommendations from the central bank. They reflect my own concerns," Quinn said. "Developments this year have been consistent with the central bank's prescription."
Quinn said Ireland's effective exchange rate was firm and the fiscal position had tightened this year.

He said Ireland's inflation performance had been encouraging so far this year but it was no longer one of the best performers in Europe on inflation and there was no room for complacency if Ireland was to meet the Maastricht criterion on inflation in 1997.
